agree.reason: A wary teller who dislikes phones gets a pay raise, first pick of shifts by seniority, and a six-month way out with full severance, so trying the role costs little, though nothing makes phone work itself appealing.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'better for everyone' claim and every figure matches the brief; only small framings such as 'Many of you also know' and the generalisation from two branches to 'our members' stretch past the facts slightly.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the raw figures without working them out: $1.50 an hour is about $3,000 a year, a 10-year teller's severance is 20 weeks of pay, and the 9-minute wait gets worse as contacts keep rising.

right_comparison.reason: It ties the status quo to the trends (44% fewer visits, 60% more contacts, 9-minute holds), but it describes the reader's other choice, severance, only as a rule and never puts it next to staying.

qualification.reason: Each condition is specific and checkable: offers by February 14, decisions by March 1, a six-month window to leave with severance, and seniority-based shift choice; the letter also states plainly that it cannot promise 9-to-5 hours.

objections.reason: It deals directly with lost 9-to-5 hours, long service and the phone team's 30% turnover, but it never answers the main objection, 'I don't want to work on the phones,' beyond offering a way out.

fit.reason: It is an email from the COO of about 420 words with a clear subject line and sections that are easy to scan, as the brief asked.
